caption: The drawing displays a single object resembling an old-fashioned oil lamp or candlestick with a handle. The object is rendered in shades of gray and is centered within a rectangular, off-white or beige background. The lamp consists of a wide, flat base that tapers into a narrower stem, which then widens again into a bell-shaped cover or reservoir with a smaller, vertical element on top, resembling a wick or adjusting knob. A curved handle is attached to the side of the stem, extending upwards and outwards before curving back down to join the base. On the lower right corner of the drawing, there is a smaller, simplified line diagram of the same object indicating measurements, with arrows showing height and width, and the artist's name "ZADENBERG" is written just below this diagram. The drawing is executed with careful shading that gives a three-dimensional appearance.
title: Lamp
cluster: #16 — Lighting Devices: Lamps, Lanterns, and Candleholders
